transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump is spending the final weeks of the midterm campaign season visiting primarily
GOP strongholds.
Today, he stumps for Republican candidates in Arizona and Montana.
Trump is banking on the GOP base to help keep Congress under Republican control.
He has suggested to voters they pretend he is on the ballot.
National polls continue to show low public approval ratings for Trump, including over
his handling of the U.S. economy.
The Labor Department reports inflation got worse last month.
More on that from NPR's Scott Horsley.
Today's inflation report is an important one because it's the last piece of a puzzle
used to calculate the cost of living adjustment that Social Security recipients will get next
year.
Now, no, benefits will go up 3.6 percent starting in January, which means the average retiree
will get an extra 75 bucks a month.
That's not a windfall, though.
It's just enough to allow people who depend on Social Security to keep treading water.
NPR's Scott Horsley.
Immigration officials are acknowledging they used a warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, for
operations.
A court order forbids converting the site into a detention center.
Details from NPR's Jasmine Garz.
Earlier this year, Homeland Security purchased 11 warehouses to turn into detention centers.
Several lawsuits by state attorneys general followed, and many of the warehouses are now
being sold.
Three of those, which the government still owns, have court orders barring conversion,
pending environmental assessments.
In recent weeks, NPR received several tips from people who believed loved ones were held
at the Roxbury warehouse.
NPR was able to speak to a young man who said he was held in the warehouse parking lot.
In a statement from ICE forwarded to NPR by the office of New Jersey Representative
Ana Lillia Mejia, officials confirmed they used the parking lot on two occasions.
They say they did not bring anyone detained into the facility.
Jasmine Garz, NPR News, New York.
Schools across the United States are experimenting with artificial intelligence in classrooms.
But Lee Gaines reports it is tough to measure whether it's helping or not.
Caitlin Shonifer is the AI specialist for Wichita Public Schools in Kansas.
She says the school system is slowly introducing students to a range of AI tools.
Last year, middle schoolers used the technology to create educational games, and some high
school students have access to an AI math tutor.
But we wrestle with what does success really mean when it comes to AI use?
Shonifer says until educators figure out how to measure the value of these AI initiatives,
these experiments will remain small in scale.
But they will continue.
We are still going ahead with caution, but with optimism with our students because it
is something that is going to impact their lives.
She says it's something they need to be educated about.
For NPR News, I'm Lee Gaines.
It's NPR News.
Students in the Albanian capital turned violent, a fire erupted outside of Albania's education
ministry.
Several people have been arrested.
More from NPR's Rob Schmitz.
The student-led demonstrations have joined an ongoing anti-government movement known as
the Flamingo Revolution, which is demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Eddie Rama
over allegations of corruption.
Rama is a vocal supporter of a luxury coastal development project linked to Jared Kushner
and Ivanka Trump that protesters say will harm the fragile coastal environment in southern
Albania.
This week, Toronto saw violent clashes between student protesters and police as demonstrators
threw stones and smashed shop windows.
Police responded with tear gas and water cannons, arresting at least 23 people.
Six police officers and one journalist were injured.
Rob Schmitz, NPR News, Washington.
Republican Congresswoman Nancy Mace's ex-fiancee and two of his business associates are charged
with sex crimes and voyeurism in South Carolina.
According to sworn statements from agents with the State Law Enforcement Division, John
Douglas Osborne is accused of crimes against a 23-year-old woman who was intoxicated and
incapacitated, while Mace's former fiancé Patrick Bryan and Eric Bernard Bowman allegedly
watched.
In an hour-long speech in the U.S. House early last year, Mace said she "accidentally uncovered
some of the most heinous crimes against women imaginable."
Mace is leaving the House this term after she lost her bid for South Carolina governor.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Trump campaigns for Republican candidates in Arizona and Montana ahead of midterms
Labor Department reports inflation worsened last month, affecting Social Security cost-of-living adjustment
Immigration officials acknowledge using Roxbury, New Jersey warehouse parking lot despite court order
Schools nationwide experiment with AI in classrooms, struggling to measure whether it helps
Student protests in Albania's capital turn violent, fire erupts outside education ministry
Toronto student protesters clash with police, 23 arrested and several injured
Nancy Mace's ex-fiancé and two associates charged with sex crimes and voyeurism in South Carolina
